Working with large datasets

Xuesong Wang

Source: vignettes/million_cell_crb_artifacts.Rmd
million_cell_crb_artifacts.Rmd

Choose an expression backend

CerebroNexus stores the expression matrix either inside the .crb or in a sparse HDF5 file next to it. Select the storage with expression_matrix_mode in exportFromSeurat() or convertSeuratToCerebro():

Mode Practical use Files to keep together
embedded Small datasets and simple single-file distribution .crb
h5 On-disk sparse expression, including single-gene queries and large datasets .crb and its recorded .h5 sidecar

An H5-backed .crb is thin: the cell names live once in the H5 file and the .crb keeps a checksum of them (see Data integrity contracts). A very large immune repertoire can also move to a third sibling, <stem>.immune.qs2 (immune_sidecar, see ?saveCerebro).

Use the benchmark guide for measured workloads and their limits. Avoid converting a large delayed or on-disk matrix into a dense matrix merely to inspect or export it.

Export, read, save and convert

This small example creates a portable CRB without downloading a dataset:

library(CerebroNexus)
cells <- c("cell-a", "cell-b", "cell-c")
object <- Cerebro$new()
object$setExpression(matrix(c(1, 0, 2, 3, 0, 4), nrow = 2,
  dimnames = list(c("gene-a", "gene-b"), cells)))
object$setMetaData(data.frame(cell_barcode = cells, sample = c("A", "A", "B")))
object$addProjection("umap", data.frame(x = 1:3, y = c(0, 1, 0), row.names = cells))
work <- tempfile("cerebro-guide-")
dir.create(work)
file <- file.path(work, "example.crb")
saveCerebro(object, file)
restored <- readCerebro(file)
stopifnot(identical(restored$getMetaData()$cell_barcode, cells))

For a prepared Seurat object, export with the required grouping/projection arguments for your dataset (see ?exportFromSeurat). For example:

exportFromSeurat(seurat_object, file = "study.crb", experiment_name = "Study",
  organism = "hg", groups = c("sample", "seurat_clusters"),
  expression_matrix_mode = "h5")

This writes study.crb and study.h5. readCerebro() reads RDS and qs2 CRBs; .crb describes the logical format, not its physical codec. saveCerebro(..., codec = "rds") requests RDS compatibility, while the default uses qs2. convertCerebro() re-serializes a CRB while reusing its existing expression data:

convertCerebro("study.crb", "study-rds.crb", codec = "rds")

convertCerebro() is also the one-time migration path for a CRB written by an older release. Such a file is rejected with uses a retired format ... Convert it once with CerebroNexus::convertCerebro(). A CRB whose expression storage this version cannot read or repair is rejected there too; re-export it from the source Seurat object with expression_matrix_mode = "h5".

Move the complete dataset

Keep paths recorded inside the CRB valid. A typical layout is:

study.crb
study.h5
study.immune.qs2   (only when the repertoire is large)
study.viewer/

Additional spatial molecule/image resources must also travel with their dataset. Do not rename or partially copy sidecars independently. RDS and qs2 versions of a CRB can share the same unchanged H5 file. The cell-order checksum stored in the .crb rejects an H5 file whose cells differ from the ones the .crb was written for.

For distribution, createShinyApp() builds a self-contained Viewer directory and copies the required resources. It resolves colliding CRB basenames and places each Viewer Pack beside the final CRB name. Follow the app creation guide.

Viewer Packs and fallback

Viewer Packs are optional derived assets for projection geometry, metadata and other prepared views. The CRB remains the source of truth. Build and validate a pack explicitly:

pack <- buildViewerPack(file, viewer_binary = "always")
stopifnot(validateViewerPack(file, pack)$valid)

Projection rows are aligned by barcode to canonical metadata order. Missing, duplicate or unmatched identities are rejected, even when row counts agree. Keep actual barcode row names on manually supplied projections.

After changing the CRB, rebuild with buildViewerPack(file, viewer_binary = "always", overwrite = TRUE). A missing, incompatible or stale pack, such as one written for another pack schema, is invalid as a whole and falls back to the ordinary data path; rebuilding it restores the fast paths. Do not suppress checksum failures or edit a manifest to make a pack appear valid.

Understand large-group plots

Violin density uses at most 4,096 mid-quantile values per group on the original measurement scale. It is an approximation and can omit rare tails. Box quartiles, median, whiskers and mean are computed separately from all finite observations; hover also reports sample count, minimum and maximum. Missing/non-finite values are excluded. Approximate density is labelled in the summary hover. Display compaction never rescales observations to force an equal mean.

Launch the demos

The installed package includes small examples:

launchCerebro(crb_file_to_load = system.file(
  "extdata", "examples", "example.crb", package = "CerebroNexus"))

The complete large-data demo

The optional complete large-data launcher requires a repository checkout. Use a checkout of a published release tag for reproducible results, and record the printed commit ID when reporting them. The launcher loads that checkout directly.

git clone https://github.com/mihem/CerebroNexus.git
cd CerebroNexus
git rev-parse HEAD
Rscript -e "install.packages(c('remotes', 'pkgload')); remotes::install_local('.', dependencies = TRUE)"
Rscript run-demo.R

These demos keep their expression matrices in H5 sidecars and need no extra package beyond the ones CerebroNexus installs.

Open http://127.0.0.1:7451. The first run downloads and prepares the official 10x one-million-neuron matrix and the Ren et al. COVID-19 immune atlas (GEO GSE158055; 1,462,702 cells, all 64 published cell populations, sample/patient clinical metadata, and 220,968 paired-TCR plus 282,464 paired-BCR cells). The initial compressed downloads total about 18 GB. The prepared H5 files are written uncompressed and take considerable disk space on top of the extracted matrices, so allow a generous amount of free cache space. Source and prepared files are cached outside the repository (set CEREBRO_LARGE_CACHE to choose the location), so later runs reuse them.

To test Ren without the 10x dataset, and to separate download/preparation failures from Viewer errors (--prepare-only exits before starting Shiny):

Rscript run-demo.R --ren-only --prepare-only
Rscript run-demo.R --ren-only --no-browser

The launcher prints the URL, the source directory and the Ren data version (currently 2), and reuses a complete compatible cache. Keep each .crb and its .h5 file together. Prepared versions use separate directories (ren/cerebro-v2/); preparation never upgrades the earlier ren/cerebro/ atlas in place, failed builds are not published, and source downloads are shared between versions.

The launcher also builds each data set’s Viewer Pack and rebuilds it when it is missing or predates an asset the viewer reads. Without a pack, the HLA & TCR motifs page spends about 15 s (about 25 s for the whole first entry) building the CDR3 Hamming-1 graph at Ren’s scale; with one, the same entry settles in under two seconds. If you start the viewer against a prepared .crb yourself, build the pack once (about a minute for Ren) with buildViewerPack("path/to/data.crb", overwrite = TRUE); rerunning it after re-preparing a CRB is also the repair.

The 10x marker-guided E18 neurogenesis path excludes endothelial, microglial and oligodendrocyte programs, orders the remaining neural lineage with early, transitional and late markers, and separates excitatory and inhibitory terminal branches. It is a labelled demonstration, not a formal trajectory-inference result. The same app also includes the bundled PBMC, immune-repertoire, trajectory, spatial, Trekker and HLA/TCR demos. See the benchmark guide before starting.

Troubleshooting

  • Missing sidecar: restore the recorded sibling .h5 (or .immune.qs2) file. A thin CRB alone is not a complete external dataset.
  • Retired format: convert the file once with convertCerebro(), or re-export a dataset whose storage this version cannot read from its source Seurat object.
  • Identity/checksum mismatch: restore the matching sidecar or re-export from a consistent source. Equal cell counts do not prove correct cell correspondence.
  • Pack rejected or slower fallback: rebuild the optional pack from the current CRB; preserve the CRB and expression data.
  • Memory pressure: inspect matrix density and format; avoid dense realization. A disk backend does not make every upstream Seurat operation out-of-core.
  • Slow first operation: distinguish package loading, backend reads and browser painting. A warm revisit is not a cold-start measurement.
